clue.text: Parallel arrangements for sleeping partners

parts.note: a couple who sleep side by side in two matching single beds rather than sharing one

explanation.surface: Someone describes how a couple's bedroom is laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeping partners' is a business term for silent investors, but here it means a couple who sleep apart, in two beds set parallel.
explanation.definitionFit: A matched pair of single beds stands side by side, parallel, for two people sharing a room.

clue.text: Scale which gives stones in pounds, ounces and grains?

definitions.text: Scale which gives stones in pounds, ounces and grains?

parts.words: Scale which gives stones in pounds, ounces and grains?
parts.note: a system of measures used for precious metals and gems, counting in pounds, ounces and grains rather than the stone

explanation.surface: A question about a set of scales for weighing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' suggests the British unit of 14 pounds, but here means gemstones, weighed in this jewellers' system of pounds, ounces and grains.
explanation.definitionFit: The jewellers' system of weights for gold, silver and gems uses a twelve-ounce pound.

clue.text: Type of ink one's getting in from the Far East

indicators.note: the second piece gets inside the ink word

parts.note: Indian ink is a dense black drawing ink
one's taken as ones

explanation.surface: Someone buys a kind of ink imported from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Something Indonesian comes from the island nation of south-east Asia, part of the Far East.

clue.text: Dealer almost ruined

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a broker deals in shares or goods for clients

explanation.surface: A trader has nearly gone bust.
explanation.definitionFit: To be broke is to have no money left, financially wiped out.

clue.text: Grumpy devil from Boulogne is awfully eager to interrupt

indicators.note: the inserted letters break into the middle of the French word

parts.note: diable is French for devil, and Boulogne is a French port
is shortened to 's, giving S

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the letters of eager are muddled

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered fiend from the French coast cuts in, horribly keen.
explanation.walkthrough: S plus AGREE (eager rearranged by 'awfully') breaks into DIABLE between DI and ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A disagreeable person is bad-tempered and unpleasant, crabby.

clue.text: Run to car a fellow's standing in front of

indicators.note: the first pieces stand ahead of the car in the answer

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man to dash to a car parked in front of him.
explanation.definitionFit: To be able to run to something is to have enough money for it, an idiom for being able to pay.

clue.text: Last to accept new spying organisation can be economic

indicators.note: the end word takes in the other pieces

parts.note: final means last
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A final round brings in a new spy agency, all about money.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic and financial both describe matters of money and the economy.

clue.text: Remove from lists -no justice

indicators.note: the letter for justice is removed

parts.note: the lists were the arena for a tournament, where knights would joust
J is the abbreviation for justice, as in a judge's title

explanation.surface: Someone is struck off a list without fair treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lists' suggests rosters, but it is the medieval tilting ground, giving JOUST; drop J.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to force them out of a place or position.

clue.text: Aim to rise about one and have a meal

indicators.note: the turned word goes round the letter for one
in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an end is an aim, a goal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone aims to get up and eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to eat dinner, the main meal.

clue.text: Oslo nerd's versatile tongue

indicators.note: versatile means turning readily, so the letters of the two words are turned into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A Norwegian geek can speak many languages.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and the medieval Scandinavian speech is one.

clue.text: College boy joined labour organisation

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A student has signed up to a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: UNISON is a large British public-sector trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade union is an organisation of workers, organised labour.

clue.text: Fieldsman owing some consideration to another

definitions.text: Fieldsman owing some consideration to another

parts.words: Fieldsman owing some consideration to another
parts.note: a man who works fields he does not own, paying rent, the consideration, to a landlord

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder is indebted to a teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fieldsman' suggests a cricket fielder; here it is a man of the fields who pays rent. 'Consideration' is the legal term for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a farmer rents land from its owner, paying rent in return for working it.

clue.text: Shrub women plant beside open space in village

parts.note: to inter is to bury, as one plants a body
a village green is the common grassy space

explanation.surface: Ladies put in a bush next to the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a noun describing the shrub, but it is the verb, to put in the ground: INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintergreen is a low evergreen bush whose leaves give an aromatic oil.

clue.text: Caretaker's set to put in appearance, turning up after next public holiday

indicators.note: the turned piece follows the holiday date

parts.note: after Christmas the next public holiday is 1 January, written Jan I

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the piece backwards
the set word takes the appearance word inside it

parts.note: a lot is a set of items, as at auction
air means appearance or manner

explanation.surface: A caretaker is due to show up again after the next bank holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: AIR goes inside LOT to make LAIROT, which is turned to TORIAL after JAN I, the date of New Year's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Janitorial describes the work of a janitor, the building's custodian, so means of a caretaker.

clue.text: Form of addiction seen in Tristan da Cunha, say?

definitions.meaning: reliance on a drug or habit
a remote South Atlantic island governed as a British overseas territory, a territory ruled from abroad

explanation.surface: Someone notices drug habits on a remote island.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliance on a substance is one sense; a territory under another state's rule is the other.

clue.text: Publication one uses for revision

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: revision means altering, so the letters of the word uses are changed in order

explanation.surface: A publication that one consults when studying for exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For revision' suggests exam study, but it signals an anagram of USES, giving SUE after I.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is one edition of a magazine or newspaper, a single printing.

clue.text: Sees Latin declension as most important

indicators.note: declension is the changing of a word's endings, so the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A pupil regards Latin grammar as the top priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declension' belongs with Latin grammar in the surface, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is indispensable, of the highest importance.

clue.text: Retrogressive separatist group detectives are to wipe out

indicators.note: going backwards, so the whole string of pieces is read from the end

parts.note: ETA was the Basque separatist group
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police are set to destroy a reactionary separatist faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrogressive' looks like a description of the group, but it turns ETA, CID and ARE all backwards: ERA DIC ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy completely, to remove every trace.

clue.text: Early advantage for Principal's doxy?

parts.note: a head is a school principal, with the possessive S
doxy is an old word for a mistress or prostitute, a tart

explanation.surface: A question about the headmaster's mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, the pieces say the head's tart, the principal's doxy.
explanation.definitionFit: A start ahead of others in a race gives a lead before anyone moves, hence any early edge.

clue.text: Old form of currency going round-it's current in Europe

indicators.note: the currency word surrounds the letter for old

parts.note: lire are the former Italian money

explanation.surface: A remark about an outdated coinage still in circulation in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks monetary after 'currency' but means a flow of water: the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The French river is a flow of water, a current, running across France.

clue.text: Worthless activity in Llandudno I've finally abandoned

indicators.note: activity means busy movement, so the letters are stirred into a new order
the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone has given up a pointless pastime in a Welsh resort.
explanation.walkthrough: LLANDUDNO plus IV (I've with its last letter, E, dropped by 'finally abandoned') are rearranged. Llandudno is a seaside town in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract declared without legal force is invalid, so the phrase means having no value or effect.

clue.text: Going up road with twelve-inch accumulation of snow

indicators.note: in a down clue going up reads the abbreviation backwards

parts.note: twelve inches is one foot, written 1 FT, read as I FT

explanation.surface: A road climbs through a foot-deep snowfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A drift is a bank of snow piled up by the wind.

clue.text: Cuba involved in South American swindle

indicators.note: the Cuba letter is wrapped inside the abbreviation

parts.note: S Am is an abbreviation for South American
C is the international vehicle code for Cuba

explanation.surface: Cuba is mixed up in a Latin American fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a fraudulent trick to cheat people of money.

clue.text: Delicate wife's quit child's game

indicators.note: the wife's letter has left the word

parts.note: wispy means fine and delicate, like thin hair
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A frail woman's partner has given up a children's pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: The guessing game in which one player names the first letter of something seen is played by children.

clue.text: Universal star originally appearing in children's publication

indicators.note: the letter shows up inside the magazine

parts.note: a comic is a magazine of strips for children

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word star

explanation.surface: A star turns up in a kids' comic and is a hit everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmic relates to the whole cosmos, so to everything there is.

clue.text: It's Caesar's fault, in the end

definitions.text: It's Caesar's fault, in the end

parts.words: It's Caesar's fault, in the end
parts.note: in Julius Caesar, Mark Antony says Brutus called Caesar ambitious, and if so it was a grievous fault; that striving finally brought his death

explanation.surface: Blame for the outcome lies with Caesar after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Antony's funeral speech in Shakespeare's play turns on the charge that Caesar was ambitious, the fault for which the conspirators killed him.
explanation.definitionFit: The trait Brutus blamed on Caesar was his drive for power, a strong desire to rise.

clue.text: Insect family, not one found to be active around end of January

indicators.note: active means moving busily, so the letters are rearranged around the added one
the word for one is taken out of the word family

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: takes the last letter of January

explanation.surface: An insect family is spotted, one member flying about in late January.
explanation.walkthrough: FAMILY loses I ('not one') to give FAMLY; add Y, the last letter of January, and rearrange. A mayfly is in fact never active in January.
explanation.definitionFit: The mayfly is a short-lived winged bug that hatches near water.

clue.text: Final indication of club rugby score, roughly

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word club

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
a tally is a running score

explanation.surface: The final scoreline of a rugby club's match, approximately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' looks like an estimate attached to the score, but it is the definition, meaning harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something brutally means doing it harshly and violently, a rough manner.
